# Transitive dependency pins for the python SDK agent e2e lane (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS
# The e2e bundle ships prebuilt from conductor-oss/python-sdk and its run.sh does a plain
# `pip install -r requirements.txt` at run time. That requirements.txt pins only
# conductor-python; everything else — pytest, langgraph, mcp-testkit, the provider SDKs —
# resolves to "whatever is newest today". So an upstream release can redden this gating lane
# with no change to this repo, and the failure looks like a server regression rather than a
# dependency bump. That is not theoretical: a langgraph/pydantic interaction with
# typing.TypedDict already breaks suite11 on Python < 3.12.
#
# HOW IT IS APPLIED
# ci.yml sets PIP_CONSTRAINT to this file. pip honours that for every install in the job,
# including the one inside the bundle's run.sh — so the bundle is pinned WITHOUT modifying it.
# Constraints only bound versions; they do not install anything.
#
# HOW TO REGENERATE (required when CONDUCTOR_PY_E2E_BUNDLE_VERSION moves)
#   cd <extracted conductor-ai-e2e-python-$VERSION>
#   uv pip compile requirements.txt \
#     --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --python-version 3.12 --no-header \
#     -o .github/agent-e2e/constraints-python.txt
#   # then re-add this header
#
# Targeted at the runner: linux x86_64, CPython 3.12 (matching setup-python in ci.yml).
# A conflict between these pins and a newer bundle's requirements surfaces as a loud pip
# resolver error at install time — which is the intent. Regenerate rather than delete.
